title: Week 3: Make it standalone
summary: The laptop steps aside. A Raspberry Pi 4 becomes the robot's brain, an EMEET speakerphone its ears and voice, and the battery from Week 2 powers everything. Then unplug it and walk away with it.
detail: Each table gets a Raspberry Pi 4 with its memory card already set up, and an EMEET M0 Plus speakerphone. The Pi runs Chrome and opens this same page, so your robot works exactly as before: enter your key and settings once and the Pi remembers them. You control the Pi from your laptop's browser while you set it up, then close the link and carry your robot away.
outcome: A robot that talks, moves its mouth and turns its head with no laptop and no wall plug, running on its own Pi and battery.
artifact: A fully wireless talking cardboard robot.
prereqs: Your robot from Week 2, with its power bank.
Your laptop, for setting up the Pi. It doesn't stay plugged in.
Everything else is on the table: a Raspberry Pi 4 and a speakerphone.

slides.title: Week 3: Make it standalone
bullets: Until now your laptop did the listening and talking.
Tonight a Raspberry Pi takes over, running on the battery you already have.
Then unplug everything and walk away with it.

slides.title: What each robot needs this week
bullets: ☐ Your robot from Week 2, with its Pico, breadboard and power bank (charged)
☐ 1 × Raspberry Pi 4, its memory card already set up
☐ 1 × EMEET M0 Plus speakerphone and its cable
☐ 1 × USB-A to micro-USB data cable, for the Pico (the Pi has USB-A ports)
☐ 1 × short cable from the power bank to the Pi's USB-C port
☐ Velcro strips or tape
☐ A card with this Pi's remote link and the room's wifi
Bring: your laptop and your Deepgram key
slides.note: Before class, set up every memory card: Raspberry Pi OS, Chromium, the room's wifi and remote screen access, with the lesson page as Chromium's home page. Write each Pi's link on its card. Test one Pi on the power bank before buying for the class: a Pi 4 wants a steady 3 A. Helper table: 2 spare ready Pis, a Pi wall power supply per table as a fallback, spare cables, spare charged power banks.

slides.title: Plug in the Pi
bullets: Speakerphone into a blue USB port on the Pi.
Unplug the Pico from your laptop and plug it into another blue port, with the USB-A cable.
Power the Pi from the power bank's other port.
Tuck the Pi and battery low inside the box and fix them with velcro or tape.
slides.note: Done when: the Pi's green light flickers and the speakerphone lights up. The battery is the heaviest part, so low in the box keeps the robot from tipping.

slides.title: Open the Pi from your laptop
bullets: On your laptop, open the Pi link on the card at your table.
You're now looking at the Pi's screen in your browser.
On the Pi, Chrome opens this lesson page.

slides.title: Set it up on the Pi
bullets: Paste your Deepgram key and connect the robot, like Week 1.
Pick the speakerphone if Chrome asks for a microphone.
Set the mouth and neck sliders again. They're saved on the Pi.
Start talking.
slides.note: The speakerphone sits right next to the robot, so keep Speaker is inside the box switched on.

slides.title: Walk away with it
bullets: Close the Pi link on your laptop.
Check nothing is plugged into a wall or a laptop.
Pick the robot up and carry it to another table. Keep talking.
slides.note: Done when: it holds a conversation on the far side of the room.

slides.title: Week 4: Demo day
bullets: Teach it a new trick and polish it.
Then show it off to guests.
Bring it fully charged.

flow.title: Run it on the Pi
flow.note: Open this page in Chrome on the Raspberry Pi, not on your laptop.

troubleshooting: Connect robot shows nothing on the Pi: the Pico cable is charge-only. Swap it for a data cable.
The robot can't hear you: in Chrome on the Pi, click the lock icon and pick the EMEET as the microphone.
No sound: set the EMEET as the Pi's audio output in the speaker menu at the top right.
The Pi link won't open: check the Pi and your laptop are on the same wifi, then ask a helper.
The Pi shows a lightning bolt or restarts: the battery port can't keep up. Try the other port or a thicker cable, or use a wall supply from the helper table for now.
The battery switches itself off: some power banks sleep on low current. Press its button to wake it.
